# R7 — Symphony early movements: 8:1–~9:14 (lines 2966–3200)

**Range read in full:** 2966–3200  
**Source:** Cockerill, *The Epistle to the Hebrews* (NICNT, 2012)  
**Evidence class default:** Cockerill as commentator on Hebrews (attributed); Scripture cited as primary when quoted.

## Claims

### C1 — Section frame: 8:1–10:18 as all-sufficient sacrifice; sanctuary/covenant/sacrifice
**Locus:** 2966–2970  
**Quote:** "Heb 8:1-10:18 discloses what he has now become through his self-offering - a High Priest \"perfected forever\" (7:28) and thus \"the Source of eternal salvation\" (5:9)… by his sacrifice the Son has atoned for sin, entered the heavenly Sanctuary as High Priest, and established the New Covenant. Thus, he uses the themes of sanctuary, covenant, and sacrifice to disclose the full magnitude of the Son's self-offering."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) 8:1–10:18 continues ch. 7: the eternal Son becomes High Priest through self-offering; delayed theme of sacrifice (announced 7:27; anticipated 1:3; 5:7–9) is explained via three interlocking themes—sanctuary, covenant, sacrifice.

### C2 — Structural metaphor: “symphony in three movements”
**Locus:** 2974  
**Quote:** "The artistry of the pastor's presentation is like a symphony in three movements (8:1-13; 9:1-22; 9:23-10:18) developing these three themes - sanctuary, sacrifice, and covenant. Each movement begins with the theme of sanctuary (8:1-2; 9:1-10; 9:23-24) and ends with covenant (8:7-13; 9:16-22; 10:15-18). At the center of each is the ever-expanding theme of sacrifice (8:3-6; 9:11-15; 9:25-10:14)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Rhetorical design of 8:1–10:18 is three movements with fixed theme order: sanctuary → sacrifice (center, expanding) → covenant; aim is cumulative persuasion so hearers persevere through Christ’s benefits (encore 10:19–25).

### C3 — Movement roles and OT framing (Ps 110; Jer 31; Ps 40 delayed)
**Locus:** 2976–2978  
**Quote:** "The first (8:1-13) lays a Scriptural foundation… Ps 110:1 and Jer 31:31-34 meant that the Son would not serve as High Priest in the earthly tabernacle or mediate the Old Covenant… he reserves Ps 40:6-8, the passage that shows the significance of Christ's sacrifice, until the heart of the third movement, found in 10:5-10."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) First movement: scriptural foundation (Ps 110:1 heavenly sanctuary; Jer 31 New Covenant; Old already obsolete by prophecy). Second (9:1–22): OT sanctuary/covenant descriptions betray insufficiency and point to Christ’s sacrifice. Third (9:23–10:18): full glory of heavenly ministry, New Covenant, and especially sacrifice (pivotal 10:5–10 / Ps 40:6–8), framed by Ps 110 and Jer 31.

### C4 — Self-offering as Day of Atonement + consecration + covenant-making
**Locus:** 2980  
**Quote:** "Christ's self-offering is, first of all, at the center of each movement… the great once-and-for-all \"Day of Atonement\" sacrifice that removes sin… also a sacrifice of high-priestly consecration that authorizes him to enter God's presence in the heavenly Sanctuary… Furthermore… a covenant-making sacrifice that establishes him as the Mediator of a new and effective way to approach God."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) One self-offering functions three ways: Day-of-Atonement sin-removal; high-priestly consecration authorizing heavenly entry; covenant-establishing sacrifice making him Mediator/Guarantor of a better covenant.

### C5 — “Main point” (8:1): High Priest seated at right hand
**Locus:** 2988–2990  
**Quote:** "1 Now this is the main point of the things being said: we have such a high priest who has sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens, 2 a minister of the Sanctuary and the true Tent that the Lord, and not any human being, has pitched… The present participle translated \"the things being said\" encompasses all that the pastor has written and has yet to write."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Heb 8:1–2 states the *main point* of the whole discourse (past and future): “we have” a High Priest seated at God’s right; pastoral aim is full appropriation of this priest (cf. 4:14–16; 10:19–25) for persevering faith.

### C6 — Session integrates eternal sonship + self-offering, not exaltation alone
**Locus:** 2992–2998  
**Quote:** "the \"High Priest who has sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens\" is not a reference limited to exaltation or session. It is a comprehensive description of the present reality available for the faithful: the one who is seated… is the eternal Son who achieved his position by offering his obedient, incarnate life up in death as an effective sacrifice for the sins of humanity."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) 8:1 assumes Ps 110:1/4 priestly session and eternal sonship already established (chs. 1; 5; 7); hearers still need explanation of how self-offering effects session as all-sufficient High Priest; “main point” is this present available reality, not mere exaltation language.

### C7 — Expanded session language: throne, “heavens,” grace
**Locus:** 3000  
**Quote:** "he expands this description: the Son has sat down at the right hand \"of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens.\" He does not add \"throne\" out of deference to contemporary speculations about a throne in the heavenly temple but in order to magnify the divine authority and sovereignty of the Son's position… \"Throne\" reminds his hearers that this \"throne\" has been made a \"throne of grace\" (4:16)"  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Intensified session phrasing magnifies authority (not temple-throne speculation); “in the heavens” anticipates heavenly locus of ministry (8:5); “throne” recalls throne of grace for hearers.

### C8 — Minister of Sanctuary and true Tent (8:2)
**Locus:** 3002–3004  
**Quote:** "he can be called \"minister of the Sanctuary and the true Tent that the Lord, and not any human being, has pitched.\" The term \"minister\" enhances the dignity and authority of this High Priest… The OT provides the foundation for identifying the heavenly dwelling place of God as the \"true\" Sanctuary replicated by the earthly Tent established by Moses… or the Temple."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) From heavenly session follows ministry in Sanctuary/true Tent pitched by the Lord, not humans; “minister” has priestly LXX usage and Hellenistic public-benefactor sense; heavenly high-priestly service benefits people by bringing them into that Sanctuary (above angelic “ministers,” 1:7, 14).

### C9 — Against Philo/Platonism: apocalyptic place of presence, not world of ideas
**Locus:** 3004–3006  
**Quote:** "Philo, however, develops it in his own Platonic way: the physical Universe is God's sanctuary accessible to the senses and a copy of his heavenly sanctuary that was accessible only to the mind… Despite many protestations to the contrary, he has little in common with Philo. The Sanctuary of Hebrews is not a heavenly sanctuary of eternal ideas perceived only by the mind through contemplation of the visible universe or the earthly Tent. The pastor speaks of the \"place\" of God's presence already entered by the incarnate and exalted Son… Unlike Philo, Hebrews never refers to the physical world using Tent imagery."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Distinguishes Hebrews from Philo/Platonic copy-of-ideas: Sanctuary is the place of God’s presence entered by the incarnate/exalted Son and open by faith/obedience; no Tent-imagery for physical cosmos; simplicity vs. elaborate Second Temple/universe-as-temple speculation.

### C10 — Sanctuary = Tent = heaven itself / Most Holy Place only (no two-part heavenly temple)
**Locus:** 3008–3010  
**Quote:** "the larger context in Hebrews suggests that the \"true Tent\" and \"the Sanctuary\" refer to the same reality… First, \"the Sanctuary\" is \"heaven itself' (9:24)… Second, this \"Sanctuary\" is clearly \"the Most Holy Place\" of God's presence \"behind the veil\" (6: 19)… Thus the Tent into which Christ has entered consists only of a Most Holy Place which is heaven itself… no conceivable purpose for a heavenly \"Holy Place\" anterior to a heavenly Most Holy Place."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Against two-part heavenly temple reading of “Sanctuary” + “Tent”: same heavenly reality—heaven itself as Most Holy Place only; earthly Holy Place (9:1–10) showed blocked access under old system; once Son enters God’s presence, no heavenly outer compartment is needed.

### C11 — Distinct connotations of “Sanctuary” vs “Tent”; “true” not “false”/Philonic
**Locus:** 3012–3016  
**Quote:** "\"Sanctuary\" designates the place entered as the very presence of the holy God of Israel… \"Tent\" provides an opportunity for asserting the superiority of this heavenly Sanctuary by contrasting it with the OT \"Tent\"… \"True\" does not condemn the Mosaic Tent as \"false.\" Nor does it identify this \"Tent\" with Philo's invisible heavenly sanctuary accessible only to the mind… \"true\" because it is the place where the salvation accomplished by Christ brings eternal fellowship with God."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Rhetorical pair: Sanctuary = close-up of holy presence entered; Tent = wide-angle for contrast with Mosaic shrine (needs qualifiers “true,” “greater and more perfect”); Mosaic Tent is transient sketch/anticipation, not “false”; Westcott right: diverse connotations, no local distinction in heavenly referent.

### C12 — Every high priest offers; Christ must offer “something” (8:3)
**Locus:** 3022–3028  
**Quote:** "3 For every high priest is established to offer gifts and sacrifices. Therefore it was necessary for this one to have something to offer… \"Something\" is intentionally general… Yet he anticipates its once-for-all character (9:25-10:4) by using a singular noun (\"something\") and an aorist verb… This \"something\" will be described… as offering \"himself without blemish to God\" (9:14) and… \"the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all\" (10:10)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Syllogism from Ps 110 session + biblical definition of high priesthood (5:1): Christ must offer; “something” is general but singular/aorist anticipates once-for-all self-offering, later filled as unblemished self (9:14) and body of Jesus once for all (10:10).

### C13 — If on earth, not a priest; law-priests in pattern and shadow (8:4–5a)
**Locus:** 3030–3034  
**Quote:** "Now if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, because there are those who offer gifts according to the law. 5 They minister in a pattern and shadow of the heavenly… Taken together, \"pattern and shadow\" underscore the derivative and merely symbolic nature of the earthly Tent… This is no \"pattern\" of eternal ideas or \"shadow\" of a timeless ministry that has always gone on in the heavenly Sanctuary. This \"pattern and shadow\" anticipated the ministry inaugurated by the exaltation of the Son"  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Contrary-to-fact: earthly location would exclude Christ from law-priesthood; earthly priests serve in “pattern and shadow” of the heavenly—inferior, symbolic, and *anticipatory* of post-exaltation ministry, not timeless Platonic ideas or always-ongoing heavenly cult.

### C14 — Exod 25:40 grounds typology; “all” anticipates 9:1–14; vs Philo on same verse
**Locus:** 3036–3040  
**Quote:** "Moses was \"solemnly instructed\" by God in Exod 25:40: \"see that you make all according to the copy given you on the [mountain]\"… \"pattern and shadow\" underscore both the insufficiency of the old as a means of salvation and its typological character as anticipation of the new… Philo understood the heavenly world of ideas… Hebrews… The Tent is no copy of the world of ideas. Rather, it prefigures the \"place\" of God's presence that Christ has entered… continued participation in the old Tent's services would be a denial of Christ's sufficiency."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Exod 25:40 (with “all” from 25:39) authorizes reading Mosaic Tent as rough reminiscence training Israel for heavenly reality; Philo uses same verse for sensible copy of noetic pattern without antiquating rituals; Hebrews: prefiguration + self-revealed inadequacy; clinging to old cult denies Christ.

### C15 — Superior ministry = Mediator of better covenant on better promises (8:6)
**Locus:** 3042–3048  
**Quote:** "But now this High Priest has obtained a ministry that is as much superior to theirs as the covenant of which he is Mediator is better, a covenant that has been legitimately established on better promises… As the \"Mediator\" of the \"better covenant\" he provides the benefits described in the \"better promises\" of Jer 31:31-34… he is not merely its \"Mediator\" but the \"Guarantor\" of its perpetual effectiveness (7:22)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Superiority of heavenly ministry measured by better covenant grounded in Jer 31 promises (benefits deferred to 10:15–18); “has obtained” stresses achievement via self-offering; vs Moses as Old Covenant mediator, Christ is both Mediator and ongoing Guarantor.

### C16 — Full Jer 31:31–34 quotation (Heb 8:8–12) and structure
**Locus:** 3052–3054  
**Quote:** "\"Behold days are coming,\" says the Lord, \"when I will complete a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. 9 It will not be like the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they did not remain in my covenant, and so I showed no concern for them,\" says the Lord. 10 \"For this is the covenant that I will covenant with the house of Israel after those days,\" says the Lord: \"I will put my laws in their minds, and inscribe them upon their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. 11 And they will not teach each his neighbor and each his brother, saying, `Know the Lord,' because all shall know me, from the least unto the greatest of them. 12 For I will be merciful toward their unrighteous deeds, and their sins I will remember no more.\""  
**Claim:** (Cockerill/Hebrews) Pastor quotes Jer 31:31–34 almost without mid-commentary; structure: announcement of “new” (v. 31 / 8:8); negative “not like” Exodus covenant because fathers did not remain (v. 32 / 8:9); positive better promises—law on heart, covenant knowledge, mercy/sin-remembrance-no-more (vv. 33–34 / 8:10–12); thrice “says the Lord” = God finds fault and promises New; no Qumran New-Covenant polemic/influence noted.

### C17 — First covenant not blameless; fault with them / wilderness generation (8:7–9)
**Locus:** 3060–3066  
**Quote:** "For if that first [covenant] had been blameless, there would have been no occasion for a second to be sought. 8 For finding fault with them he says… It is their failure that evidences the insufficiency of the Old Covenant… not their inability to obey but their refusal to obey that demonstrates the insufficiency of the first covenant to adequately transform the human heart… The \"fathers\"… can be none other than the rebellious wilderness generation described in 3:7-4:11… \"did not remain\" in it… By implication, the promised New Covenant will be one that provides resources that enable his people to \"remain.\""  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Mere prophecy of a second covenant proves first not blameless (cf. Melchizedek priesthood in 7:11); restraint vs stronger anti-priesthood language because fault is with people (wilderness fathers); refusal-to-obey, not metaphysical inability; New Covenant supplies resources to “remain”; pastoral bridge from 3:7–4:11 warning to ch. 11 faithfulness.

### C18 — Textual nuance: “complete/perfect” New vs mere “make” of Old
**Locus:** 3070  
**Quote:** "Hebrews uses a stronger word for God's establishing the New Covenant in Jer 31:31 (Heb 8:8), and a weaker when speaking of his establishing the old in Jer 31:32 (Heb 8:9)… God will \"accomplish,\" \"fulfill,\" \"perfect,\" or \"complete\" the New Covenant… related to the pastor's favorite terms - \"perfect\" and \"perfection.\"… simply \"the first covenant which I made.\""  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Significant LXX-to-Hebrews variation: stronger verb for New (“complete/perfect”) vs weaker “make” for Old anticipates New’s sufficiency and perfection theme.

### C19 — Better promises outline (heart, fellowship, sin-removal); postponed to 10:15–18
**Locus:** 3072  
**Quote:** "This second half of the Jeremiah passage outlines the interlocking benefits of the New Covenant that address the deficit of the Old - a willing obedience springing from God's laws written on the heart, intimate fellowship with God, and the removal of sin… \"after these days\" has been inaugurated by the High Priest at God's right hand who has come \"at the end of these days\" (1:2)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Three interlocking New-Covenant benefits: internalized law/obedience, intimate knowledge of God, sin-removal/mercy; inaugurated at “end of these days” by seated High Priest; full exposition deferred until after sacrificial teaching (10:15–18).

### C20 — Obsolescence by saying “new” (8:13); type remains
**Locus:** 3052, 3074  
**Quote:** "13 By saying \"new\" he makes the first obsolete. What is becoming obsolete and growing old is on the verge of passing away… The pastor is speaking from Jeremiah's point of view. As soon as God promised a \"new\" covenant, the Old was \"near to passing [away].\" Since the New has come in Christ, the Old is no longer \"near to\" but has definitively passed away as a way of relating to God… The Old Covenant continues only as a type of the New."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) God’s mere declaration “new” brands first obsolete/old; Jeremiah’s vantage: already near vanishing; post-Christ: definitively passed as way of relating to God; persists only typologically—transition to 9:1–10 on old Tent’s impotence.

### C21 — Second movement key shift: sanctuary/covenant minor; sacrifice major
**Locus:** 3080  
**Quote:** "In the second movement… we hear \"sanctuary\" and \"covenant\" in a minor key but \"sacrifice\" in major. The pastor/conductor describes the old sanctuary (9:1-10) and the establishing of the Old Covenant (9:16-22) in order to expose their insufficiency and their preparatory character. On the other hand he vigorously affirms the unfathomable efficacy of Christ's sacrifice… able to \"cleanse the conscience\" (9:11-15)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) 9:1–22 reverses first-movement emphasis: looks back at Pentateuchal earthly sanctuary and Old Covenant founding as preparatory/inadequate; focuses all-sufficient quality of Christ’s sacrifice (cleansing conscience).

### C22 — Earthly sanctuary: regulations + structure dual significance (9:1–10)
**Locus:** 3084–3088  
**Quote:** "I On the other hand, then, the first covenant was having regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary… Verses 2-5 describe this sanctuary, and vv. 6-7 the First-Covenant worship… Verses 8-10 conclude by unveiling the significance… intended by the Holy Spirit… First, they demonstrate the impossibility of approaching God through the old sanctuary. Second, they anticipate the \"new and living way\" (10:20) of approach to God through Christ."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Unity of 9:1–10: announce topic → describe furniture → describe worship → Spirit’s meaning; structure determines liturgy; dual role—impossibility of approach under old + anticipation of Christ.

### C23 — “Earthly” sanctuary qualified vs unqualified heavenly Sanctuary
**Locus:** 3090–3092  
**Quote:** "Just as the pastor never uses \"Tent\" for the heavenly reality without a qualifying description, so he never uses \"Sanctuary\" for the earthly copy without qualification - \"an earthly sanctuary\" (9:1); \"a sanctuary made by hand\" (9:24)… limited because it is part of the temporal, created universe and thus can provide no access to the Creator… singular… inferiority of the earthly sanctuary… one structure despite… first and second tents"  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Linguistic asymmetry: heavenly Tent needs qualifiers; earthly Sanctuary always qualified (“earthly,” “made by hand”); singular “sanctuary” marks inferior one structure even when split as first/second tents for argument.

### C24 — Tabernacle furniture: Holy Place lampstand, table, bread (9:2)
**Locus:** 3094–3096  
**Quote:** "A Tent had been prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand and the table and the presentation of bread. This Tent was called the Holy Place… described as if its two parts were two separate \"Tents\" - a \"First\" and a \"Second\"… The impenetrable barrier between the two is vital to his argument."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Outer “First Tent” = Holy Place with lampstand (Exod 25:31–40) and table/presentation bread (Exod 25:23–30; Lev 24:9); rhetorical two-tent description maximizes Holy/Most Holy divide and blocked access.

### C25 — Most Holy Place: incense altar association, Ark contents, Cherubim/Mercy Seat (9:3–5)
**Locus:** 3098–3112  
**Quote:** "But after the second curtain was a Tent called the Most Holy Place, 4 having an incense altar covered with gold and the Ark of the Covenant covered all over with gold, in which were a golden jar containing manna and Aaron's rod that budded and the tablets of the covenant. 5 Above the Ark were the Cherubim of Glory overshadowing the mercy seat… It seems clear that the pastor is referring to the Altar of Incense and not to a censer… He does not \"relocate\" this altar within the inner sanctuary but closely associates it with the Most Holy Place in accord with its function… climaxes… Cherubim of Glory overshadowing the Mercy Seat… place of atonement in anticipation of fulfillment in Christ… true \"Mercy Seat.\""  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Inner description magnifies golden majesty: incense altar (not mere censer) functionally associated with Most Holy Place (Day of Atonement coals/blood; Exod 30:10; Lev 16) without ignorant relocation; Ark holds tablets, manna jar (LXX golden), Aaron’s rod; climax Cherubim of Glory / Mercy Seat as earthly throne and atonement locus foreshadowing Christ’s entry and throne of grace.

### C26 — Day of Atonement pattern in old high-priest entry (9:6–7)
**Locus:** 3116–3122  
**Quote:** "the priests regularly entered the first Tent… but into the second once a year the high priest alone not without blood which he offered for himself and for the people's sins of ignorance… continuous, repetitive… never achieve even symbolic access… \"Only\" the \"high priest\"… \"once a year\"… also… the pattern for Christ's high-priestly ministry… \"once a year\"… symbolic of Christ's entrance \"once for all\"… \"not without blood\" anticipated Christ's entrance \"through his own blood\" (v. 12)"  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Outer ministry = endless repetition confined to First Tent; inner = alone, annual, blood for self and people—proves insufficiency yet typologically patterns Christ’s once-for-all entry through his own blood and self-offering for the people (not himself as sin-bearer in Aaronic sense).

### C27 — Holy Spirit’s lesson: way into Sanctuary closed while First Tent valid (9:8)
**Locus:** 3124–3128  
**Quote:** "By this the Holy Spirit is showing that the way into the Sanctuary was not yet revealed while that First Tent still had validity… \"Sanctuary\" refers not to the earthly Most Holy Place but to the heavenly \"Sanctuary\"… \"First Tent,\" however, refers to the first part of the Mosaic shrine, the Holy Place… The First or Old Covenant was a covenant of the Holy Place… the New Covenant has no Holy Place but only the Most Holy Place that is \"heaven itself' (9:24)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Spirit (Scripture’s inspirer) discloses from plain OT description: heavenly Sanctuary access not revealed while Holy Place (“First Tent”) was in force; Old = Holy-Place religion; high priest’s annual entry is exception proving the rule; New has only Most Holy Place = heaven itself.

### C28 — First Tent as “parable”; gifts/sacrifices cannot perfect conscience (9:9–10)
**Locus:** 3130–3136  
**Quote:** "That Tent was a parable for the time then present. In relation to that Tent gifts and sacrifices were offered which were not able to perfect the worshipers in regard to their conscience. 10 Those gifts and sacrifices pertained only to food and drink and various washings, regulations of the flesh, established until the time of correction… essence of the human predicament is an \"evil heart of unbelief'… The sacrifices of the First Tent belonged to the same sphere as these ceremonial regulations… valid… only \"until the time of correction\" when Christ \"arrived as High Priest of the good things that have come\" (v. 11)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Holy Place symbolizes pre-Christ lack of access (“parable for the time then present”); all gifts/sacrifices fail to perfect/cleanse conscience (= heart/inner person); only fleshly/ceremonial purity (food, drink, washings) until “time of correction” (= Christ establishing New).

### C29 — Link: no cleansing → no heavenly access; sets up 9:11–15
**Locus:** 3138  
**Quote:** "Only those who have been forgiven and cleansed from sin so that they now live in faithful obedience are able to enjoy such communion with our holy God… By his obedient sacrifice Christ can \"cleanse\" the conscience (9:14) from the impurity of sin and write God's laws on his people's hearts as promised in the New Covenant (10:15-18)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Intrinsic link between conscience-cleansing and heavenly access; 9:9–10 prepares 9:11–15 and New-Covenant heart-writing.

### C30 — Christ High Priest of good things that have come; greater/more perfect Tent (9:11)
**Locus:** 3142, 3156–3164  
**Quote:** "But Christ has arrived as High Priest of the good things that have come through the greater and more perfect Tent not made with hands, which is not of this creation… \"But Christ,\" show that these verses stand in sharp contrast with vv. 1-10… reading \"good things\" that \"have come\"… present cleansing from sin and access to God… \"Greater\" and \"more perfect\"… nothing less than the Sanctuary Christ has entered… \"not made with hands, that is, not a part of this creation,\" it can be nothing other than the Tent that \"God, not man, built,\" called the \"true Tent\" in 8:2."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Sharp contrast: Christ arrives as High Priest of inaugurated “good things that have come” (prefers aorist reading over “to come”; present cleansing/access without excluding heavenly homeland); pathway/locus = greater, more perfect, uncreated Tent = 8:2 true Tent; no need for heavenly Holy Place.

### C31 — Rejects intermediate-heaven and body-as-Tent readings of 9:11
**Locus:** 3166–3170  
**Quote:** "Some have attempted to identify this \"greater and more perfect Tent\"… as the physical heavens… physical heavens are part of the creation… Andriessen… \"intermediate\" heaven… superfluous… Others… metaphor for the body of Christ… \"through\" parallel to \"by means of his own blood\"… inadequate… one can hardly say that Christ's \"body\" was \"not of this creation\"… no contextual clues… identify this \"Tent\" with the \"true Tent and Sanctuary\" in which Christ ministers (8:2)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Against (1) physical/intermediate heavens as the Tent (created / argumentatively superfluous) and (2) body-of-Christ metaphor (instrumental *dia* forced by parallel, no context, “not of this creation” problem): Tent = true Sanctuary of 8:2.

### C32 — Entered once for all by own blood, not goats/calves; eternal redemption (9:12)
**Locus:** 3142, 3172–3178  
**Quote:** "He entered once for all into the Sanctuary not by means of the blood of goats and calves but by means of his own blood, having obtained eternal redemption… The shed blood of \"goats and calves\" represented the lives… Christ's \"own [blood]\". His shed \"blood\" is his willing offering of his life through death on the cross… careful to avoid giving the impression that Christ carried his blood into heaven… entered heaven \"by means of his blood\" shed on the cross… \"having obtained eternal redemption\"… means or cause of his entrance… not… subsequent… NRSV… liberation from the corruption of sin… and thus from the fear of death and judgment… \"eternal\" in its effectiveness, benefits, and duration."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Means of entry = own blood = life offered in death on the cross (Lev 17:11 analogy), not animal blood; once-for-all aorists; does *not* carry blood into heaven or complete offering by heavenly sprinkling—session confirms cross; eternal redemption = costly liberation from sin’s bondage (deeper than Exodus), means of entrance not afterthought.

### C33 — A fortiori: animal blood / heifer ashes purify flesh; Christ’s blood cleanses conscience (9:13–14)
**Locus:** 3180–3186  
**Quote:** "For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on the participants sanctify for the purification of the flesh, 14 by how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself blameless to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!… lasting value as a type or anticipation of the true cleansing… whole sacrificial system was restricted to outward purification… main clause… what Christ's \"blood\" can do: \"cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God.\""  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Classic lesser-to-greater: Day-of-Atonement animals + Num 19 heifer ashes = flesh purification / community worship access, typological of true cleansing; “how much more” Christ’s blood cleanses conscience from dead works unto service of living God; expands beyond single Day-of-Atonement pair to all old sacrifices’ impotency (order/word shifts goats-calves / goats-bulls).

### C34 — “Through the eternal Spirit… offered himself blameless”
**Locus:** 3188–3196  
**Quote:** "Christ's sacrifice was effective because it was offered \"through the eternal Spirit.\"… probably… Holy Spirit, but without diminution of all that he has said about the Son's eternal being… \"eternal\" evokes… eternal sonship… \"by the power of an indestructible life\" (7:16)… Spirit… in the Son's incarnate life… \"blameless\"… often used to describe the \"goats and bulls\"… without physical blemish… incarnate obedience… without moral blemish… anticipates… 10:5-10"  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Efficacy grounds: (1) eternal Spirit (likely Holy Spirit; anarthrous stress on eternal quality; complements indestructible-life priesthood; Spirit in incarnate obedience, no wedge vs Son); (2) blameless self-offering—cultic unblemished term moralized by earthly obedience; anticipates 10:5–10 climax.

### C35 — Conscience cleansing: from dead works to serve living God; not OT rituals as “dead works”
**Locus:** 3198–3200  
**Quote:** "the blood of Christ \"cleanses our conscience from dead works to serve the living God.\"… not a cleansing of the body or of the \"flesh\" but of the \"conscience\"… \"heart\"… \"Cleansing\" the conscience and \"perfecting\" (v. 9 above) the conscience refer to the same reality… \"dead works\"… not referring to the rituals of the Old Covenant but to the sin from which those rituals could not cleanse… equivalent of idolatry… result in falling \"away from the living God\" (3:12)… purged… replaced by God's \"laws\" (10:15-18) written on the heart"  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Definitive benefit statement so far: cleanses *conscience* (inner/heart; same reality as “perfect” conscience) *from dead works* (= sin/unbelief’s fruit, not Levitical rites as such) *to serve living God*; yields moral-spiritual transformation and New-Covenant law-on-heart obedience; received in union with seated High Priest as source of eternal salvation.

### C36 — 9:15 hinge: sacrifice makes him Mediator of New Covenant (edge of range)
**Locus:** 3142, 3148  
**Quote:** "And on account of this he has become Mediator of a New Covenant, so that, since a death has occurred for redemption of the transgressions committed under the First Covenant, those who have been called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance… v. 15 draws a concluding inference from vv. 11-14… mirror image of 8:6… both conclude the sacrifice section… and provide transitions to the covenant section"  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Because of all-sufficient atoning sacrifice, Christ becomes New-Covenant Mediator; death redeems First-Covenant transgressions so the called receive eternal inheritance; 9:15 // 8:6 close sacrifice units and open covenant units in movements 1–2. (Range ends mid-discussion of 9:14/edge of 9:15; 9:16–22 largely beyond slice.)

### C37 — First-movement close: heavenly Sanctuary + New Covenant prove different sacrifice
**Locus:** 3076  
**Quote:** "Thus the heavenly Sanctuary, in which, according to Ps 110:1, this High Priest exercises his ministry (vv. 1-2), and the \"new\" covenant of Jer 31:31-34, which he administers (vv. 7-13), both demonstrate that his sacrifice must have been different from and superior to those offered in the earthly Tent (vv. 3-6)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Movement 1 conclusion: Ps 110 sanctuary locus + Jer 31 covenant together necessitate a sacrifice different from/superior to earthly Tent offerings—audience left eager for nature of difference (answered from 9:1 onward).

### C38 — Typology load-bearing: old insufficient yet anticipatory (pattern/shadow/parable)
**Locus:** 3034, 3074, 3086, 3180  
**Quote:** "\"pattern and shadow\"… anticipated the ministry inaugurated by the exaltation of the Son… The Old Covenant continues only as a type of the New… anticipate the \"new and living way\" (10:20)… lasting value as a type or anticipation of the true cleansing available through the blood of Christ."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Unified typological hermeneutic across 8–9: Mosaic sanctuary/covenant/sacrifice are simultaneously insufficient means of salvation and God-designed anticipations (pattern/shadow/type/parable) of Christ’s heavenly entry, New Covenant, and conscience-cleansing blood—not discarded history nor Philonic eternal forms.

## Coverage

**Read:** lines 2966–3200 complete (sequential).  
**In range:** Symphony program (8:1–10:18); first movement 8:1–13 complete (main point; Sanctuary/true Tent; different sacrifice; Exod 25:40; better covenant; full Jer 31:31–34; obsolescence 8:13); second-movement intro; 9:1–10 earthly tent/furniture/Day of Atonement liturgy/Spirit’s parable/conscience; 9:11–14 (into 9:15) Christ High Priest of good things, greater Tent, own blood vs goats, eternal redemption, eternal Spirit, conscience cleansing.  
**Beyond range / only framed:** full 9:16–22 covenant blood inauguration; third movement 9:23–10:18; Ps 40:6–8 / 10:5–10; full Jer re-use 10:15–18.
